vsm2.14:25.1:
Knowledge about enunciation of language dealing with meaning and law (§21): there is the language that is individual
essence, the usage that has no exceptions, and deals with that meaning and that law.
vsm2.14:25.2:
Any knowledge falling within the category concerned with the enunciation of that, with the speaking,
with the utterance of that, concerned with the root-speech of all beings, the Magadhan language that is individual
essence, in other words, the language of law (dhamma), any knowledge that as soon as it hears it spoken, pronounced,
uttered, knows, "This is the individual-essence language; this is not the individual-essence language"—
vsm2.14:25.3: such knowledge is discrimination of language.
vsm2.14:25.4:
One who has reached the discrimination of language knows, on hearing the words "phasso,
vedanā," etc., that that is the individual-essence language,
vsm2.14:25.5: and on hearing "phassā, vedano," etc., he knows that that is not the individual-essence language.
vsm2.14:26.1:
Knowledge about kinds of knowledge (§21): when a man is reviewing and makes any of the foregoing kinds of knowledge
the object of his knowledge, then any knowledge in him that has knowledge as its object is discrimination of perspicuity,
vsm2.14:26.2:
and so is any knowledge about these aforesaid kinds of knowledge,
which is concerned with details of their individual domains, functions, and so on.
vsm2.14:27.1: And these four kinds of discrimination can be placed in two categories: the plane of the trainer and the plane of the non-trainer.
vsm2.14:27.2: Herein, those of the chief disciples and great disciples come into the category of the non-trainer's plane.
vsm2.14:27.3:
Those of the Elder Ānanda, the householder Citta, the layman Dhammika, the householder Upāli,
the laywoman Khujjuttarā, etc., come into the category of the trainer's plane.
vsm2.14:28.1:
And though they come into the categories of the two planes thus, they are nevertheless distinguishable in five aspects,
that is to say, as achievement, mastery of scriptures, hearing, questioning, and prior effort.
vsm2.14:28.2: Herein, achievement is the reaching of Arahantship.
vsm2.14:28.3: Mastery of scriptures is mastery of the Buddha's word.
vsm2.14:28.4: Hearing is learning the Dhamma carefully and attentively.
vsm2.14:28.5: Questioning is discussion of knotty passages and explanatory passages in the texts, commentaries, and so on.
vsm2.14:28.6:
Prior effort is devotion to insight in the dispensation of former Buddhas, up to the vicinity of the stages of conformity
and change-of-lineage by one who has practiced the duty of going with the meditation subject on alms round and coming back with it.
vsm2.14:29.2: A prior effort, and great knowledge, / Knowledge of dialects, of scriptures,
vsm2.14:29.3: And questioning, and then achievement, / And likewise waiting on a teacher,
vsm2.14:29.4: Success in friends—these are conditions / Productive of discriminations.
vsm2.14:30.1: Herein, prior effort is the same as that already stated.
vsm2.14:30.2: Great learning is skill in some science or sphere of craft.
vsm2.14:30.3: Dialects means skill in the hundred-and-one tongues,
vsm2.14:30.5: Scriptures means mastery of the Buddha's word, even if only of the Chapter of Similes.
vsm2.14:30.6: Questioning is questioning about defining the meaning of even a single stanza.
vsm2.14:30.8: Waiting on a teacher is living with very learned intelligent teachers.
vsm2.14:30.9: Success in friends is acquisition of friends such as that.
vsm2.14:31.1: Herein, Buddhas and Paccekabuddhas reach the discriminations through prior effort and through achievement.
vsm2.14:31.2: Disciples do so through all these means.
vsm2.14:31.3: And there is no special way of developing a meditation subject in order to attain discriminations.
vsm2.14:31.4: But in trainers the attaining of the discriminations comes about next upon the liberation consisting in trainers' fruition,
vsm2.14:31.5: and in non-trainers it does so next upon the liberation consisting in non-trainers' fruition.
vsm2.14:31.6: For the discriminations come to success in Noble Ones only through the noble fruition as the ten powers do in Perfect Ones.
vsm2.14:31.7: So these were the discriminations referred to when it was said above: "It is of four kinds … as the four discriminations" (§8).
vsm2.14:32.2:
Now, the things classed as aggregates, bases, elements, faculties, truths,
dependent origination, etc., are the soil of this understanding,
vsm2.14:32.3: and the first two purifications, namely, purification of virtue and purification of consciousness, are its roots,
vsm2.14:32.5:
Consequently, one who is perfecting these should first fortify his knowledge by learning and questioning
about those things that are the "soil" after he has perfected the two purifications that are the "roots,"
then he can develop the five purifications that are the "trunk."
vsm2.14:33.1:
B. DESCRIPTION OF THE FIVE AGGREGATES When it was said above "the things classed as aggregates,
bases, elements, faculties, truths, dependent origination, etc., are the soil,"
vsm2.14:33.2:
the aggregates here are the five aggregates, that is to say, the materiality aggregate, the feeling aggregate,
the perception aggregate, the formations aggregate, and the consciousness aggregate.
vsm2.14:34.1:
34. Herein, all kinds of states whatsoever that have the characteristic of "being molested" (ruppana) by cold,
etc., taken all together should be understood as the materiality (rūpa) aggregate.
vsm2.14:34.2: 1. That is of one kind with the characteristic of "being molested."
vsm2.14:34.3: 2. It is also of two kinds when classed as (a) primary entity (bhūta) and (b) derived by clinging (upādāya).
vsm2.14:35.1: Herein (a) primary materiality is of four kinds as the earth element, water element, fire element, and air element.
vsm2.14:35.2: Their characteristic, function, and manifestation have been given under the definition of the four elements (XI.87, 93);
vsm2.14:35.3: but as to the proximate cause, each has the other three as its proximate cause.
vsm2.14:36.1: (b) Derived materiality is of twenty-four kinds as eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, visible datum, sound, odour, flavour;
vsm2.14:36.2: femininity faculty, masculinity faculty, life faculty, heart-basis;
vsm2.14:36.3: bodily intimation, verbal intimation; space element;
vsm2.14:36.4:
lightness of matter, malleability of matter, wieldiness of matter, growth of matter, continuity of matter,
ageing of matter, impermanence of matter, and physical nutriment.
vsm2.14:37.1:
1. Herein, the eye's characteristic is sensitivity of primary elements that is ready for the impact of visible
data; or its characteristic is sensitivity of primary elements originated by kamma sourcing from desire to see.
vsm2.14:37.2: Its function is to pick up an object among visible data.
vsm2.14:37.3: It is manifested as the footing of eye-consciousness.
vsm2.14:37.4: Its proximate cause is primary elements born of kamma sourcing from desire to see.
vsm2.14:38.1:
2. The ear's characteristic is sensitivity of primary elements that is ready for the impact of sounds; or its characteristic
is sensitivity of primary elements originated by kamma sourcing from desire to hear.
vsm2.14:38.2: Its function is to pick up an object among sounds.
vsm2.14:38.3: It is manifested as the footing of ear-consciousness.
vsm2.14:38.4: Its proximate cause is primary elements born of kamma sourcing from desire to hear.
vsm2.14:39.1:
3. The nose's characteristic is sensitivity of primary elements that is ready for the impact of odours; or its characteristic
is sensitivity of primary elements originated by kamma sourcing from desire to smell.
vsm2.14:39.2: Its function is to pick up an object among odours.
vsm2.14:39.3: It is manifested as the footing of nose-consciousness.
vsm2.14:39.4: Its proximate cause is primary elements born of kamma sourcing from desire to smell.
vsm2.14:40.1:
4. The tongue's characteristic is sensitivity of primary elements that is ready for the impact of flavours; or its characteristic
is sensitivity of primary elements originated by kamma sourcing from desire to taste.
vsm2.14:40.2: Its function is to pick up an object among flavours.
vsm2.14:40.3: It is manifested as the footing of tongue-consciousness.
vsm2.14:40.4: Its proximate cause is primary elements born of kamma sourcing from desire to taste.
vsm2.14:41.1:
5. The body's characteristic is sensitivity of primary elements that is ready for the impact of tangible
data; or its characteristic is sensitivity of primary elements originated by kamma sourcing from desire to touch.
vsm2.14:41.2: Its function is to pick up an object among tangible data.
vsm2.14:41.3: It is manifested as the footing of body-consciousness.
vsm2.14:41.4: Its proximate cause is primary elements born of kamma sourcing from desire to touch.
vsm2.14:42.1:
Some, however, say that the eye is sensitivity of primary elements that have fire in excess, and that the ear,
nose, and tongue are sensitivity of primary elements that have respectively air,
earth, and water in excess, and that the body is that of all four equally.
vsm2.14:42.2:
Others say that the eye is sensitivity of those that have fire in excess, and that the ear, nose,
tongue, and body are sensitivity of those that have respectively aperture, air, water, and earth in excess.
vsm2.14:42.3: They should be asked to quote a sutta.
vsm2.14:42.4: They will certainly not find one.
vsm2.14:43.1:
But some give as their reason that it is because these several sensitivities are respectively
aided by visible data, etc., as qualities of fire, and so on.
vsm2.14:43.2: They should be asked, "But who has said that visible data, etc., are qualities of fire and so on?
vsm2.14:43.3:
For it is not possible to say of primary elements, which remain always inseparable,
that 'This is a quality of this one, that is a quality of that one.'"
vsm2.14:44.1:
Then they may say: "Just as you assume, from excess of some primary element in such and such material things,
the respective functions of upholding (sandhāraṇa), etc., for earth, etc.,
vsm2.14:44.2:
so from finding visibility, etc., respectively in a state of excess in material things that have fire in excess,
one may assume that visible data, etc., are respectively qualities of these."
vsm2.14:44.3:
They should be told: "We might assume it if there were more odour in cotton,
which has earth in excess, than in fermented liquor, which has water in excess,
vsm2.14:44.4: and if the colour of cold water were weaker than the colour of hot water, which has heat in excess."
vsm2.14:45.1:
But since neither of these is a fact, you should therefore give up conjecturing
the difference to be in the supporting primary elements.
vsm2.14:45.2:
Just as the natures of visible objects, etc., are dissimilar from each other though there
is no difference in the primaries that form a single group, so too are eye-sensitivity, etc.,
though no other cause of their difference exists. This is how it should be taken.
vsm2.14:45.3: But what is it that is not common to them all?
vsm2.14:45.4: It is the kamma itself that is the reason for their difference.
vsm2.14:45.5: Therefore their difference is due to difference of kamma, not to difference of primary elements;
vsm2.14:45.6: for if there were difference of primary elements, sensitivity itself would not arise,
vsm2.14:45.7: since the Ancients have said: "Sensitivity is of those that are equal, not of those that are unequal."
vsm2.14:46.1:
Now, among these sensitivities thus possessed of difference due to difference of kamma,
the eye and the ear apprehend non-contiguous objective fields,
vsm2.14:46.2:
since consciousness is caused even if the supporting primaries of the objective fields
do not adhere to the faculties' own supporting primaries.
vsm2.14:46.3: The nose, tongue and body apprehend contiguous objective fields,
vsm2.14:46.4:
because consciousness is caused only if their objective fields' primaries adhere to their own supporting primaries,
that is to say, if the objective fields' primaries adhere as support in the case of odours and flavours, and themselves
directly in the case of tangible data, which are identical with the three primaries excluding water.
vsm2.14:47.1:
1. There is what is called the "eye" in the world. That looks like a blue lotus
petal and is surrounded by black eyelashes and varied with dark and light circles.
vsm2.14:47.2:
The eye sensitivity as meant here is to be found in the place in the middle of the black circle surrounded by the white circle
in that feature of the eye with its accessories where there appears the image of the bodies of those who stand in front of it.
vsm2.14:47.3: It pervades the eye's seven layers like oil sprinkled on seven layers of cotton.
vsm2.14:47.4:
It is assisted by the four primary elements whose respective functions are upholding, cohering, maturing, and moving,
as a warrior prince is by four nurses whose functions are holding, bathing, dressing, and fanning.
vsm2.14:47.5:
It is consolidated by temperature, consciousness, and nutriment; it is maintained by life;
it is furnished with colour, odour, flavour, etc. (see Ch. XVIII, §5);
vsm2.14:47.6: it is the size of a mere louse's head;
vsm2.14:47.7:
and it duly serves both as physical basis and as door for eye-consciousness,
and the rest of the consciousness of the cognitive series.
vsm2.14:48.1: And this is said by the General of the Dhamma:
vsm2.14:48.2: "The sensitivity with which he sees a visible object
vsm2.14:48.3: Is small and it is subtle, too, no bigger, than a louse's head."(?)
vsm2.14:49.1:
2. The ear sensitivity is to be found inside the feature of the ear-hole with its accessories in the place
that is shaped like a finger-stall and surrounded by fine brown hairs.
vsm2.14:49.2: It is assisted by the elements in the way aforesaid.
vsm2.14:49.3: It is consolidated by temperature, consciousness, and nutriment; it is maintained by life; it is equipped with colour, etc.;
vsm2.14:49.4: and it duly serves both as physical basis and as door for ear-consciousness, and the rest.
vsm2.14:50.1:
3. The nose sensitivity is to be found inside the feature of the nose-hole
with its accessories in the place shaped like a goat's hoof.
vsm2.14:50.2: It has assistance, consolidation and maintenance in the way aforesaid;
vsm2.14:50.3: and it duly serves both as physical basis and as door for nose-consciousness, and the rest.
vsm2.14:51.1:
4. The tongue sensitivity is to be found in the middle of the feature of the tongue
with its accessories in the place shaped like a lotus petal tip.
vsm2.14:51.2: It has assistance, consolidation and maintenance in the way aforesaid;
vsm2.14:51.3: and it duly serves both as physical basis and as door for tongue-consciousness, and the rest.
vsm2.14:52.1:
5. The body sensitivity is to be found everywhere, like a liquid that soaks a layer of cotton, in this
physical body where there is matter that is clung to.
vsm2.14:52.2: It has assistance, consolidation and maintenance in the way aforesaid too;
vsm2.14:52.3: and it duly serves both as physical basis and as door for body-consciousness, and the rest.
vsm2.14:53.1:
Like snakes, crocodiles, birds, dogs, and jackals that gravitate to their own respective resorts,
that is to say, termite-mounds, water, space, villages, and charnel grounds, so the eye, etc., should be regarded
as gravitating to their own respective resorts, that is to say, visible data, and so on (cf. Dhs-a 314).
vsm2.14:54.1: 6. As regards visible data, etc., which come next, a visible datum has the characteristic of impinging on the eye.
vsm2.14:54.2: Its function is to be the objective field of eye-consciousness.
vsm2.14:54.3: It is manifested as the resort of that too.
vsm2.14:54.4: Its proximate cause is the four great primaries.
vsm2.14:54.5: And all the following kinds of derived materiality are the same as this.
vsm2.14:54.6: Where there is a difference we shall mention it.
vsm2.14:54.7: This visible datum is of various kinds as "blue, yellow" (Dhs §617) and so on.
vsm2.14:55.1: 7. Sound has the characteristic of impinging on the ear.
vsm2.14:55.2: Its function is to be the object of ear-consciousness.
vsm2.14:55.3: It is manifested as the resort of that too.
vsm2.14:55.4: It is of various kinds as "drum sound, tabour sound" (Dhs §621) and so on.
vsm2.14:56.1: 8. Odour has the characteristic of impinging on the nose.
vsm2.14:56.2: Its function is to be the object of nose-consciousness.
vsm2.14:56.3: It is manifested as the resort of that too.
vsm2.14:56.4: It is of various kinds as "root odour, heartwood odour" (Dhs §625) and so on.
vsm2.14:57.1: 9. Flavour has the characteristic of impinging on the tongue.
vsm2.14:57.2: Its function is to be the object of tongue-consciousness.
vsm2.14:57.3: It is manifested as the resort of that too.
vsm2.14:57.4: It is of various kinds as "root flavour, trunk flavour" (Dhs §629) and so on.
vsm2.14:58.1: 10. The femininity faculty has the female sex as its characteristic.
vsm2.14:58.2: Its function is to show that "this is a female."
vsm2.14:58.3: It is manifested as the reason for the mark, sign, work, and ways of the female (cf. Dhs §633).
vsm2.14:58.4: 11. The masculinity faculty has the male sex as its characteristic.
vsm2.14:58.5: Its function is to show that "this is a male."
vsm2.14:58.6: It is manifested as the reason for the mark, sign, work, and ways of the male (cf. Dhs §634).
vsm2.14:58.7: Both these last are coextensive with the whole body, as body-sensitivity is.
vsm2.14:58.8:
But it does not follow that they have to be called either "located in the space where
body-sensitivity is located" or "located in the space where that is not located."
vsm2.14:58.9: Like the natures of visible data, etc., these are not confoundable one with the other.
